correctness.rationale: An independent direct computation on the full complex, not relying on the supplied collapse sequence, constructs the specified 16-vertex, 24-edge graph and the metric by Floyd–Warshall. A triple is forbidden iff the sum of its three pairwise distances is twice their maximum, exactly the geodesic betweenness test. Exhaustive subset generation finds 336 forbidden triples and 16,120,224,220,80 faces in dimensions 0–4, none in dimension 5 and hence none above. The signed full boundary matrices satisfy ∂²=0, have ranks 15,81,139,80 in degrees 1–4, and have only unit nonzero integer Smith factors. Thus every boundary image is saturated in its chain group and also in the cycle subgroup. The full unreduced chain groups give reduced ranks (0,24,4,1,0), and no torsion. The complete 1-skeleton confirms connectedness. This corroborates the frozen proof even without reproducing its optional shorter chain complex; the attached collapse logic also checks unique codimension-one cofaces in a simplicial complex. No conclusion about a wedge splitting follows or is needed.
residual_risks: The calculation is limited to the exact graph and the chosen geodesic definition; no integral homotopy classification.

The matching complex has graph edges for vertices. A metric Rips complex either omits some edges in its 1-skeleton or is a full simplex, unlike this general-position complex.
On the same cubic graph, an open or closed neighborhood complex cannot have faces of size five, unlike this complex; the catalog Kneser hit is not even GP(8,3).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same metric or base graph does not imply equality of the underlying simplicial complexes or their homology. GP(8,3), Möbius–Kantor and the incidence graph of the (8_3) configuration denote the same base graph in this review.

value.rationale: The general-position functor is motivated independently by graph betweenness and the graph is the canonical small cubic symmetric graph of the (8_3) configuration, not a selected parameter chosen for an easy computation. Its exact answer is a concrete mixed-dimension and torsion-free benchmark for geodesic complexes: even the full face counts do not show the simultaneous nonvanishing in degrees 1, 2 and 3 or rule out torsion. The finite result answers both questions completely without overstating a homotopy consequence.
residual_risks: Single graph only; no inferred family, automorphism module or attaching-map classification.
